SELECTED_INDEX: 6
CONFIDENCE: 0.26
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by 3 strong C–H stretching bands near 2972-2926-2880 cm⁻¹ and a single strong C=O stretch at 1714 cm⁻¹, typical of a saturated, unconjugated aliphatic ketone.  A very intense CH₂-rocking band appears at 720 cm⁻¹, which is characteristic of a straight (CH₂)ₙ segment of four or more consecutive methylenes; this favours a linear or nearly linear chain rather than a cyclic structure.  Additional CH₂/CH₃ deformation bands are present at 1458, 1349 and 1305 cm⁻¹, and C–C / C–O skeletal modes for an aliphatic ketone occur at 1235-1181-1108-1054 cm⁻¹ together with medium-weak bands at 956-920-872 cm⁻¹.  

Among the candidates, compound 6 (CCCC(=O)CCC) is a simple, unbranched (CH₂)₄–CO–(CH₂)₂ chain ketone whose Raman profile matches all the key features:  
• carbonyl at ~1715 cm⁻¹,  
• long CH₂ sequence giving the strong 720 cm⁻¹ rocker,  
• no strong bands that would signify O–H (acid) or O–CH₃ (methoxy) groups that are absent in the spectrum.  

Therefore candidate 6 provides the best overall agreement with the observed Raman peaks.
